step_by_step_reasoning: The whiteboard architecture depicts a serverless data ingestion and analytics pipeline for high-volume travel event tracking at Intent. 1. External web/mobile users send events via JavaScript through API Gateway, while backend ad services in ECS send events using KPL to a primary Kinesis Data Stream. 2. A event processor Lambda consumes events from Kinesis, referencing schema definitions stored in a top S3 bucket. 3. Processed events are published to a secondary Kinesis stream (processed streams) serving as integration points. 4. Kinesis Data Firehose delivers these events into an S3 bucket (data lake). 5. A batch deduplication and conversion process reorganizes data on S3 into Parquet format. 6. Data scientists and analysts query the transformed data in S3 directly using Amazon Athena.

nodes.name: Lambda (Processor)
nodes.notes: Processes events by schema fingerprinting and schema validation from S3

nodes.name: Kinesis Stream (Processed)
nodes.notes: Processed event streams used as downstream integration points

nodes.name: Kinesis Data Firehose
nodes.notes: Streams processed events into S3 data lake storage

nodes.notes: Stores raw Avro files and converted Parquet partitions

nodes.notes: Interactive query engine for analytics on Parquet data

nodes.name: Data Scientists & Analysts
nodes.notes: Queries data using Athena for experiments and ad-hoc analytics

edges.notes: Web JavaScript sends user activity events to API Gateway
API Gateway forwards event data into Kinesis Stream
ECS services write event streams using KPL to Kinesis Stream
Processor Lambdas trigger on incoming Kinesis events
Lambda reads schema and reference data from S3
Lambda publishes decoded and processed events to secondary Kinesis stream
Processed Kinesis stream feeds into Kinesis Firehose
Firehose writes raw event files into S3
Batch process deduplicates and converts Avro files to Parquet back in S3
Athena queries formatted Parquet data stored in S3
Data scientists and analysts consume query results from Athena
